_comment: THE WORKOUT LINK REGISTRY — every short /w/ link that gets pasted into a TrainingPeaks workout. Added September 5, 2026. READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A CODE. (1) A code maps to a library.json `key`, NOT to a URL. The destination is resolved per athlete at request time from library.json's `memberUrl` for THAT ATHLETE'S OWN LANGUAGE — so one link pasted once into a library workout sends a Spanish athlete to /members/activacion/ and an English athlete to /members/en/activation/. This is why the registry holds a key and not a path, and why adding a fourth inventory of URLs would have been the wrong build: library.json already owns every destination in three languages. (2) `slot` is the WORKOUT CONTEXT the link was pasted into, not a second destination — activacion-run and activacion-bike both 302 to the same artifact and differ only in what the log records. That is the point of tool+slot: the destination is the tool, the code is where the click came from, and a code cannot be added retroactively to a workout already frozen into a published plan. (3) A TrainingPeaks plan is a STATIC SNAPSHOT — whatever is pasted is permanent across every future application of that plan — which is why these are short owned paths and not UTM-tagged member URLs. A UTM on a gated URL is inert anyway: Caddy's `redir * /members/<lang>/login?next={http.request.orig_uri}` nests the whole query string inside `next=`, and GA4 does not parse it (ai-infrastructure-documentation.md, Sept 2 addendum). (4) tests/workout-links.test.js fails the build if a code names a key that is not live in library.json, or if a gated live tool has no code at all — that second assertion exists because a tool shipping without its inventory row has now failed three times (cyclistcore Aug 24, strength Sep 2, hombro Sep 3).
_slotVocabulary: Keep slots short and reusable. Established: pre, post, vo2, umbral, largo, test, semana (descarga), carrera, hotel/viaje, run, bike, swim, fuerza. A new slot is fine; a synonym for an existing one is not.
